composer.name: Maurice Ravel
composer.bio: French master of orchestral colour and pianistic precision. His solo piano works range from limpid early miniatures to the terrifying virtuosity of Gaspard de la nuit — every note exactly weighted, nothing wasted.
composer.license: Public domain (Ravel died 1937; works PD in most countries). Individual engravings/editions may carry separate typesetting rights — check each IMSLP page.
composer.catalogNote: Complete solo-piano works (plus Ma mère l'Oye, piano four-hands, flagged). Orchestral works, ballets, songs and chamber music from the full 84-work IMSLP category are excluded.

pieces.title: Sérénade grotesque
pieces.story: Ravel's earliest surviving piano piece, written around eighteen. Guitar-like strummed chords and Spanish snap already point to the mature composer of Alborada.

pieces.title: Menuet antique
pieces.story: Ravel's first published work. An 'antique' minuet seen through modern, slightly acid harmony — later orchestrated by the composer.

pieces.title: Pavane pour une infante défunte
pieces.story: A 'pavane for a dead princess' — not a lament for anyone real, but for a stately Spanish court dance imagined from the past. Ravel warned pianists not to drag it: 'It is a pavane, not a dead princess.'

pieces.title: Jeux d'eau
pieces.story: 'Play of water' — fountains, cascades and rivulets rendered in glittering figuration. It reinvented piano texture and opened the door to musical Impressionism at the keyboard.

pieces.title: Sonatine
pieces.story: A jewel of classical proportion and restraint. Begun for a competition that was cancelled, it distils sonata form into three tightly linked movements built from one falling-fourth motif.

pieces.title: Miroirs
pieces.story: Five 'mirrors' — moths, sad birds, a boat on the ocean, a jester's dawn serenade, a valley of bells. Each dedicated to a member of Ravel's artistic circle, the 'Apaches'.

pieces.title: Gaspard de la nuit
pieces.story: Three poems of the night by Aloysius Bertrand made into piano music of legendary difficulty. Ravel set out to write something 'more difficult than Balakirev's Islamey' — and Scarbo delivers.

pieces.title: Menuet sur le nom d'Haydn
pieces.story: A miniature tribute built from the notes spelling H-A-Y-D-N, written for the centenary of Haydn's death alongside pieces by Debussy and others.

pieces.title: Ma mère l'Oye (suite)
movements: Pavane de la Belle au bois dormant
Les entretiens de la Belle et de la Bête
pieces.story: 'Mother Goose' — fairy-tale scenes written for two children to play as a duet. Deceptively simple on the page, exquisitely coloured in sound.

pieces.title: Valses nobles et sentimentales
pieces.story: Eight waltzes 'noble and sentimental', after Schubert. First performed anonymously at a concert where the audience was invited to guess the composer — most guessed wrong.

pieces.title: À la manière de Borodine
pieces.story: An affectionate pastiche 'in the manner of Borodin' — a lilting waltz that gently imitates the Russian master's style.

pieces.title: À la manière de Chabrier
pieces.story: A paraphrase of a tune from Gounod's Faust rewritten as Chabrier might have — a witty, loving impersonation of a fellow Frenchman.

pieces.title: Prélude
pieces.story: A tiny sight-reading test written for the Paris Conservatoire. Under a minute long, it is the gentlest possible entry into Ravel's piano writing.

pieces.title: Le tombeau de Couperin
pieces.story: A Baroque-style suite that is also a war memorial — each movement dedicated to a friend killed in the First World War. Elegant on the surface, grief underneath.
